record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal and KL results for a weight-edit implementation of directional ablation, rather than the original paper's activation projection intervention.
record.gate_note: The README describes residual-geometry plots and a sample geometry table, but does not report those as tests of whether a direction causally mediates refusal. The table of model evaluations reports refusal rates and KL divergence for the listed models.
record.test_reason: This fork reproduces the upstream p-e-w/heretic README. Heretic is a tool that applies abliteration, a weight-edit form of directional ablation. Its only results are its own tool's performance against other abliterations on gemma-3-12b-it: 3/100 refusals and KL 0.16, with the direction and ablation kernel chosen by optimization. It does not test whether a single difference-in-means direction mediates refusal: there is no addition experiment, no fixed-direction ablation, and no capability benchmark. The numbers are also not this fork's own; they are copied from the upstream repository. It relies on the finding as a tool and reports tool performance, which is T4.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right; one correction. The README says Heretic, run automatically, matches other abliterations' refusal suppression (3/100) at much lower KL (0.16 vs 0.45 and 1.04), which it reads as less damage to capabilities. The correction: these are the upstream p-e-w/heretic author's claims reproduced in this fork, not results produced by the fork.
record.recipe_differences: Uses per-layer difference-of-means directions from first-token residuals, then orthogonalizes selected attention out-projection and MLP down-projection matrices. It optimizes ablation parameters and reports weight-edited model evaluations; it does not report the original activation-projection or addition experiments. This is a tool repository, identified in its description as a fork of p-e-w/heretic.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says direction choice and ablation weights are optimized separately for components; it also states that MLP interventions tend to be more damaging than attention interventions. No outcome comparisons for these settings are reported in the README.
record.problems: The README reports a single Heretic-generated model in the evaluation table. The KL divergence is an indirect measure of preservation, not a direct capability benchmark. No uncertainty estimates or controls are reported.

untested.parts: Inducing refusal by adding the direction; ablating a single fixed difference-in-means direction; preservation of general capability on benchmarks.
Not tested as a study: there is one tool-generated model with numbers copied from upstream, and no controls or uncertainty.

record.verdict_notes: This is a fork, described as 'fork of p-e-w/heretic', with an unmodified README, so any evidence belongs to the upstream repository and should not be counted twice. The residual-geometry table for gemma-3-270m-it is descriptive only: cosines and norms of mean and median directions, plus silhouette scores. It has no causal or refusal-rate measure and bears on no version. User testimonials are anecdotal. The tool's optimized, interpolated direction index means the edited models do not isolate one difference-in-means direction.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test adding the direction to induce refusals. Does not project it out of every layer and position, and KL divergence is not a direct test of general capability.
The README reports one Heretic-generated model; it does not establish results for released models generally.

rows.subject: p-e-w/gemma-3-12b-it-heretic
rows.operation_detail: Heretic directional-ablation weight edit; the README reports model evaluation, not code execution in this repository.
rows.note: The README says the Heretic result achieves the same level of refusal suppression as the compared abliterations.
rows.check: Not a V1 test: the direction is optimized, interpolating between per-layer directions, and the layer kernel is tuned, so this is not ablation of one fixed direction. As tool performance (97/100 to 3/100) it shows practical removal, but the figure is copied from upstream and the optimizer co-minimizes refusals, so it is a selection value; the evaluation prompts may overlap the optimization prompts (not stated).
